hypotheses.rationale: High dispatch_queue (mean ~35, max 45) indicates dispatch service backlog; most orders are open and undelivered in the 60-min window (q1,q2). A saturated dispatcher would cause assignment delays and high bad_order_rate.

If dispatch calls are hanging (dependency latency) they would pile up in the dispatch queue and prevent assignments, producing similar high queue and open orders; queue metrics alone may not distinguish slow service from saturation.
If many couriers are offline, orders would remain unassigned and open; however that alone wouldn't necessarily cause a large dispatch_queue unless dispatch retries or checks queue up.

steps.response: recorded 3 hypotheses

args.rationale: If dispatcher_saturation is true, increasing workers should reduce bad_order_rate by lowering dispatch_queue; if dispatch_latency (hang) is true, more workers won't help and bad rate won't drop.

steps.response:
[evidence x3] lab experiment from t=290.0: set_dispatcher_workers vs control, 2 paired replicas, cohort = orders accepted in the next 90 min, outcomes at +150 min.

mean click-to-door (penalised) control 91.2 -> treatment 36.3 min (diff -54.9, 95% CI -55.7..-54.1)
cost 5.00 units; remaining 5.00

args.summary: Experimentally increasing dispatcher workers sharply reduced bad_order_rate (diff -0.948, CI -0.975..-0.921) and click-to-door times; high dispatch queue preceded the alert (mean ~35). Conclusion: dispatcher saturation caused assignment delays and bad orders. Recommendation: increase dispatcher workers to 10 to restore capacity.

Only 52 couriers online and 39.5 idle, so reduced supply could contribute to assignment and pickup delay.
This restaurant has the highest kitchen load (5.2) and its historical orders show high bad rate, making a scoped prep delay plausible.
Fast failed dispatches with retries could inflate queue and bad orders, though current gauges do not directly distinguish this.
Hanging dispatch calls could also create queueing without failures; queue evidence alone does not separate it.
